correctness.rationale: On a connected graph every nonfixed period-three state has all vertices rotating: any nonrotator stays zero and cannot border a rotator. Rotation requires each initial vertex to have a successor-color neighbor. Conditional on a coloring, each possible edge can support only the lower cyclic-color endpoint, making the deficiency indicators exactly independent Bernoulli. Multinomial conditioning gives the finite formula. Uniform color-class concentration and rare-event Poisson approximation give B_n -> Poisson(w e^-t) in total variation. A component union bound proves G(n,p) is connected with high probability at the critical window. Integer-weight exhaustive checks for n<=5 and direct seeded simulations confirm the formulas without serving as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: A rarest-initial-color bottleneck produces a sharp logarithmic random-graph critical window and explicit Poisson zero-mass for *immediate* primitive-three recurrent states, distinct from earlier eventual-oscillation thresholds on a 1/n scale. The exact finite-size conditional law and the nonuniform-color coefficient w provide a motivated structural dynamical statistic beyond a local color check. The threshold resolves a natural probability question for a fully specified infinite family of random networks.
